{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The kitchen had kept its cold the way the attic had kept its dust. She set the lamp on the table and did not light the stove, and Tomas did not ask her to. He stood by the door with his hands at his sides, a man waiting to be told whether he was a guest or something else.

"There's tea," she said. "If it hasn't turned to powder."

"It has. I bought it for him in the spring. He never opened it."

She found the tin anyway and pried the lid and breathed in what was left of the smell. It was faint and a little like hay. She put two spoons in the pot and filled it from the kettle that was still, somehow, half full of yesterday's water, and the whole small ceremony of it steadied her more than she wanted to admit.

The drip over the stairwell had found its rhythm now. She counted it without meaning to.

"You'll want to see the ledger," Tomas said.

"Is it bad?"

"It's honest. He paid me when he could and wrote down when he couldn't. I never held him to it."

"I will."

He looked at her then, properly, for the first time since she had come up the road with the rain in her collar. She could not tell if what crossed his face was relief or the beginning of an argument he had decided not to have.

"That's yours to decide," he said. "It's your roof now."

She poured the tea. It was weak and grey and she drank it anyway, standing, while the house went on letting the weather in one drop at a time."}
